**Finding: compliant (at/above fallback) — no redline proposed.**

Section 18.9 works for us: it is mutual, and we may assign without Array's consent to an acquirer of substantially all of our business or assets by merger, acquisition or otherwise (subject only to the acquirer's written assumption). Affiliate assignments require consent that may not be unreasonably withheld or delayed — the playbook fallback rather than the preferred consent-free affiliate right — and the general Third Party consent standard is unqualified, but both are symmetric and are minor sub-elements rather than material failures.

On change of control, there is no walk-away trigger: Section 18.10 only imposes firewall obligations on Array following a **Change in Control of Array**, and Section 4.5(b) similarly terminates only on Array's Change in Control. Nothing in the termination article (Art. XIII, including 13.4 bankruptcy) gives Array a right to terminate, re-price or renegotiate on an Ono change of control.
